outcome.technical: One rule in the shared split (_config.split_heredocs): a body left as data goes to _written_body_runs, which reads the paths the heredoc's own command writes (redirect targets on its line read outside quotes via a new _plain_mask that _shell_level now uses with identical output; tee operands) against every later clause: the path as program word past wrappers, the script operand or < input of a shell, source, . or interpreter (never an argument the script is handed), the path inside an interpreter's inline program, the same inside eval or a shell -c, and names cp/mv/ln/install/tee give the file. Paths compare by last component; an expansion matches any path except a bare PATH-looked-up program word when the written path is the expansion. Interpreter run puts the body in code, any other run in shell. No guard code changed; runnable_text/parts/clauses unchanged. Cases: hb15 and hb16 (test__config), gh36, s84 and s85, gu56, gr75. Gate sweep 6/6 files, 1768 cases, exit 0; other _config importers and source lints 8/8 files, 1240 cases, exit 0. Probe matrix over main, HEAD and this tree: HEAD to fix weaker 0 in all four guards; main to fix weaker 172 guard-by-case rows: house-form allows allow1-4, replay rows b11/b12, b2/b2b reset rows in hist (allowed already at HEAD; main's deny was a phantom cd reason), and the written-never-run .sh rows wa1/wa2/wa3/wa5 (the gh35 class the rule keeps as data). Every written-then-run shape is graded by all four guards. Dependants: every _config importer still correct (split_heredocs signature and return shape unchanged, more bodies graded only for written-then-run shapes, effective_cwd unreadable for those), their suites green; guard-history-rewrite and guard-secrets-read code unchanged; guard-uncommitted and guard-release gained one selftest case each; test files gained cases only.
outcome.descriptive: A heredoc written to a file that a later clause of the same command runs is graded as that run's program by all four guards; a body written to a file nothing runs stays data.
